title: Lug and pin joint calculator
summary: Preliminary static sizing of a double-shear lug and pin joint (one male lug between two identical female clevis legs, one solid pin) under axial, transverse or oblique ultimate tension load, following the AFFDL Stress Analysis Manual (1986), chapter 9.
disclaimer: Preliminary-sizing tool only. It is not a certified stress analysis and has not been checked against Bruhn or Niu. Coefficients K, Kn, hav/D, Ktru, Ktry, B and B0.05 are keyed in by you from the manual's figures; the results are only as good as those readings and the material allowables. Check every result independently before relying on it for design, manufacture or airworthiness.
units: Stored canonically in N, mm and MPa (N/mm²). Strains and coefficients are dimensionless. The unit switches change display and entry only, so saved files and links stay valid in any units.
method: Yield cap = ultimate factor ÷ fitting factor (1.5 ÷ 1.15 = 1.304, the constant printed in Eqs. 9-3, 9-6 and 9-9).

Each member: axial bearing (Eqs. 9-1 to 9-3), net-section tension (Eqs. 9-4 to 9-6) and their minimum Pu.L (Eq. 9-7); transverse bearing (Eqs. 9-28 to 9-30); the oblique allowable from (P/Pu.L)^1.6 + (Ptr/Ptru.L)^1.6 = 1 (Eq. 9-31); the bushing (Eqs. 9-8, 9-9); and the lug-bushing strength (Eq. 9-10).

Joint: Pu.L.B = min(2·Pu.L.B.1, Pu.L.B.2) (Eq. 9-11), pin double shear (Eq. 9-12), pin bending with uniform bearing (Eqs. 9-13 to 9-15), the load-shift refinement when the pin is weak in bending (Eqs. 9-16 to 9-18), the joint allowable Pall (Eq. 9-19a or 9-19b), and the tangs (Eq. 9-20, or Eq. 9-22 when Eq. 9-19b governs).
Under oblique load each member's oblique allowable replaces its axial lug strength in Eq. 9-10 (Sec. 9.11); the bushing is still checked (Sec. 9.10.2) and the pin takes the full resultant.
If εu < 5% and B and B0.05 are entered, bearing allowables (axial and transverse) are multiplied by B/B0.05 (Sec. 9.15).

Ultimate FS = capped allowable ÷ (P_ult × fitting factor × additional factor). Yield FS = uncapped yield allowable ÷ (P_ult ÷ ultimate factor × fitting factor × additional factor). MS = FS − 1. The pin and the tangs have ultimate checks only.
Each female leg carries half the load; the female tang row covers both legs together.
assumptions: Tension side only; α from 0° (axial) to 90° (transverse).
Full-radius, concentric ends: e = w/2 and a = e − D/2.
The tangs are checked for the axial component P·cos α only. This is an assumption of this tool, not a statement of the manual.

The oblique FS is [(P/Pu.L)^1.6 + (Ptr/Ptru.L)^1.6]^(−1/1.6), derived algebraically from Eq. 9-31; it matches the reserve-factor form (exponent 1.6, power 0.625) in the INCAS Bulletin paper listed in the sources.
The constants 1.571, 0.0982 and 0.1963 of Eqs. 9-12, 9-14 and 9-15 are used as π/2, π/32 and π/16.
not_in_scope: Hollow pins, pin yield and press-fit stresses
D/t > 5: the Fig. 9-3 bearing efficiency factor is not applied (a warning is shown instead)

reference_notes.text: Eq. 9-5 prints Fny.L = Ku·Fty. Ku is not defined anywhere in the chapter; it is read as Kn, the net-tension coefficient of Eq. 9-4.

Sec. 9.6 example, female net-section tension: the printed line is Pnu.L = 2 × 1.304 × 0.74 × 40000 × (2.5 − 1.0) × 0.5 = 57,898 lbs. Eq. 9-6b for one leg gives 28,949 lbs (the printed value is the pair of legs). It does not govern and is not asserted.

Sec. 9.6 example, male net-section tension: the printed line applies Eq. 9-6b (1.304 × 0.87 × 66000 × 2.0 × 0.75 = 112,313 lbs), but Ftu = 77,000 psi ≤ 1.304 × 66,000 = 86,064 psi, so Eq. 9-6a applies: 0.87 × 77000 × 2.0 × 0.75 = 100,485 lbs. It does not govern and is not asserted.
Sec. 9.6 example, male bearing: 1.33 × 77000 × 1.00 × 0.75 evaluates to 76,808 lbs; the example prints 77,000 lbs. Not asserted.

Eq. 9-18b prints 2b2.min = Pub.P.max·t2 ÷ (2·Pu.L.B.2), but the Sec. 9.6 example evaluates 37900 × 0.75 ÷ 44000 = 0.646 in, without the 2. The example's form is the one consistent with the male lug carrying the full load, and it is the one used here.

Eq. 9-19b takes Pall = min(Pus.P, Pub.P.max) and does not say what happens when Pub.P.max exceeds the full-thickness lug-bushing strength Pu.L.B. Then b1.min > t1 or 2b2.min > t2 and the load-shift refinement is not valid. This tool takes Pall = min(Pus.P, Pub.P.max, Pu.L.B), clamps b1.min to t1 and 2b2.min to t2 for Eq. 9-22a, and shows a warning. The Sec. 9.6 example is unaffected (Pub.P.max = 37,900 lbs < Pu.L.B = 44,000 lbs).
Sec. 9.6 example, C: the printed denominator reads 286 × 0.75 + 44000 × 0.050; the numbers that give the printed 29,000 lbs/in are 28600 × 0.75 + 44000 × 0.50.
Sec. 9.6 example, female tangs (Eq. 9-22a): the printed bracket reads (0.1 − 0.331/0.500); Eq. 9-22a and the printed result 92,700 lbs need (1 − 0.331/0.500).

Table 9-1 gives no Fbru or Fbry at e/D = 2.0 or tang allowables. The example preset uses Ftu.T = Ftux of each lug, and typical plate bearing values (2024-T351: Fbru 128 ksi, Fbry 83 ksi; 7075-T651: Fbru 148 ksi, Fbry 106 ksi) only so the e/D = 2.0 bearing limit has something to check; they do not govern. The applied load of 30,000 lbf is also this tool's choice, not the manual's.
Bruhn's and Niu's own equation numbering has not been verified, so the Bruhn/Niu column of the trace starts empty and every formula is flagged “not cross-checked” until a reference is entered.
